title: ARC-AGI-2
hook: ARC-AGI-2 rebuilt the abstraction benchmark to defeat brute-force search — frontier models that aced version 1 initially scored near zero, while humans still solve it.
key_points: Second version of the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus from the ARC Prize team (2025).
Tasks require inferring novel rules from a few examples — no memorizable training data helps.
Designed to resist the brute-force program search that cracked ARC-AGI-1.
Major labs now report ARC-AGI-2 scores; it remains a rare unsaturated reasoning benchmark.
content_html: ARC-AGI-2 is the second iteration of the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus, the benchmark built around François Chollet's argument that intelligence is skill-acquisition efficiency, not memorized skill. Each task gives a few input-output grid examples and asks the solver to infer the underlying rule and apply it to a new case — puzzles with little in common with web-scale training data.
extra_html:
How it works

Version 2 was rebuilt specifically to close the loopholes that let systems crack the original: it curates tasks that resist brute-force program search and that don't yield to pattern-matching against training data, providing a more granular signal of genuine abstract reasoning. When it launched, frontier models that had posted high numbers on ARC-AGI-1 dropped to very low scores, while average humans still solved a majority of tasks — a deliberate gap.

Why it matters

Most benchmarks saturate: models reach ceiling and the test stops discriminating. ARC-AGI-2 was engineered to keep separating systems precisely where it matters — novel reasoning rather than recall — which is why the major labs began reporting scores on it and why it became a closely watched proxy for real generalization rather than memorization.

related.title: On the Measure of Intelligence (ARC)
related.hook: Is a high benchmark score the same as intelligence? Chollet argues no — intelligence is how efficiently you acquire new skills, not how well you perform known ones.

related.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro: Frontier Reasoning (2026)
related.hook: Gemini 3.1 Pro pushes core reasoning past the Gemini 3 Pro baseline, scoring 77.1% verified on ARC-AGI-2 - a benchmark built to resist the memorization that inflates other scores.

related.title: Chatbot Arena: Ranking LLMs by Human Preference
related.hook: How do you rank chatbots when there's no single right answer? Let people pick the better of two anonymous replies, then aggregate the votes into a leaderboard.
